subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 04, 2026
body:
geocode-glib conflict resolved in acreetionos + acreetionos-xlibre

If your maps broke after a recent update, the fix is in. The geocode-glib update conflict that was breaking location services on installed systems has been resolved with a clean merge from the repair branch, and it is already rolling out to active systems.

Development
The conflict came from a version mismatch between geocode-glib and its dependencies after the last sync. Natalie and Darren tracked it down, patched it, and merged the fix into both acreetionos and acreetionos-xlibre. If you are seeing location failures in your desktop apps, a full system update should clear it up. On the packaging side, cobra3282000 has also contributed a new firefox-fix package that restores window position saving on Linux, which has been a quiet annoyance for a while. You can follow the full details in the changelog.

Community
In broader open-source news, openSUSE Leap 16.1 landed this week with a unified traditional and immutable model, and Fedora 45 shipped with all its editions. Security updates also dropped Tuesday for AlmaLinux and related RPM-based systems, covering kernel, Firefox, and several other packages. If you are juggling multiple distros like many of us do, these are worth a glance even if AcreetionOS stays on its own steady track.

Tip of the day
If you want to see exactly what changed before you update, point your browser at the changelog and filter by the packages you care about. It is faster than reading through hundreds of lines of upstream release notes, and it keeps your Friday afternoon from turning into a debugging session.
